name: Balanced k-Way Graph Partitioning
problem_statement: Given an undirected graph and a target part count k, assign every vertex to exactly one of k parts of approximately equal size so that the total weight of edges crossing between parts is minimized.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Remove self-loops; they never cross a partition boundary.
Collapse parallel edges by summing nonnegative weights; use unit weight when edge_weight_mode=unweighted.

problem_inputs.name: balance_mode
problem_inputs.description: Whether a part's size is measured by vertex count or by the sum of declared vertex weights.

problem_inputs.name: imbalance_tolerance
problem_inputs.description: Maximum allowed fractional deviation of any part's size from the ideal average size (e.g. 0.03 permits up to 3% imbalance).

problem_inputs.name: edge_weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: Use unit edge cost or declared nonnegative edge weights for the cut objective.

problem_inputs.name: objective
problem_inputs.description: Minimize total crossing edge weight, or total crossing edge weight normalized by part size (conductance-style objective).

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Balanced partitioning is NP-hard; approximate (heuristic, multilevel) solutions are the norm beyond tiny graphs.

required_outputs.name: partition_assignment
required_outputs.description: Part index in [0, num_parts) assigned to every vertex.

required_outputs.name: objective_value
required_outputs.description: Achieved value of the selected objective (edge_cut or normalized_cut).

required_outputs.name: part_sizes
required_outputs.description: Size of each part under balance_mode, indexed by part number.

required_outputs.name: balanced
required_outputs.description: Whether every part's size is within imbalance_tolerance of the ideal average.

optional_outputs.name: imbalance_ratio
optional_outputs.description: Maximum achieved fractional deviation of any part's size from the ideal average.

optional_outputs.name: cut_edges
optional_outputs.description: Edges whose endpoints fall in different parts.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Disclosed bound or gap-to-best-known for an approximate result, when available.

solution_semantics.objective: Minimize objective_value over partition_assignment subject to every part's balance_mode size being within imbalance_tolerance of the ideal average size (total size divided by num_parts).
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires optimal=true and is only expected to terminate on small graphs; approximate mode must disclose imbalance_ratio and, when known, approximation_bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each vertex is assigned to exactly one part.
solution_semantics.ordering: Part indices are an arbitrary stable labeling, not a ranking.

validation_rules: Every vertex appears in partition_assignment with exactly one part index in [0, num_parts).
part_sizes recomputes exactly from partition_assignment and balance_mode.
objective_value recomputes exactly from partition_assignment, cut_edges, and the normalized graph.
balanced=true only when every entry of part_sizes is within imbalance_tolerance of the ideal average.
edge_cases: num_parts equal to vertex_count makes every part a single vertex with objective_value equal to the total edge weight.
num_parts == 1 is rejected; a single-part result is trivial and not a meaningful partitioning request.

A connected component much larger than the ideal part size forces either splitting that component or accepting it cannot be perfectly balanced within imbalance_tolerance; the latter must be reported via balanced=false rather than silently relaxed.
Isolated vertices may be assigned to any part to help satisfy balance without affecting objective_value.

correctness: assignment completeness (every vertex assigned exactly once)
